analysis.title: Tech selloff sends investors into Treasuries
key_insights: A tech stock selloff pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory and drove safe-haven demand for Treasuries, with the 10-year yield down 19 bps to 4.95% for the week.
The Bloomberg U.S. Treasury Index gained 1.28%. Longer-duration, rate-sensitive sectors led: taxable munis +1.57%, agency MBS +1.41%, U.S. Aggregate +1.18%.
The curve steepened: 2-year fell 20 bps to 4.65%, 5-year fell 22 bps to 4.74%, 10-year fell 19 bps to 4.95%, 30-year fell 14 bps to 5.33%.
Credit lagged as spreads widened: IG +10 bps to 96, high yield +51 to 367, EM debt +37 to 219. High yield returned -0.86% and EM debt -0.65%.

Nuveen still expects Fed hikes in December 2026 and now also in March 2027, followed by a pause to assess whether inflation is easing. Strong inflation, steady growth and a stable job market support this.
Nuveen forecasts the 10-year yield at 4.95% at end-2026 and 4.75% at end-2027, and the 2-year at 4.70% and 4.50% for the same dates.

The firm favors high-quality bonds with attractive yields and says credit fundamentals remain sound despite wider spreads. In munis it favors longer duration over Treasuries, with muni yields at 4.29%.

High yield was hit by the equity selloff and heavy new issuance, with fund flows turning negative and lower-rated credits lagging. IG corporates returned 0.84% as lower Treasury yields offset wider spreads.
Senior loans returned -0.09%, outperforming high yield bonds, with low duration limiting the rally benefit. CLO and loan fund demand was steady and flows were positive, led by CLO ETFs.
Securitized credit gained on lower rates: MBS +1.41% (spread 34 bps), CMBS +1.03% (72 bps), ABS +0.66% (52 bps). Senior CLO tranches held firm while lower-rated tranches varied.
EM debt fell despite lower Treasury yields as hard currency spreads widened and the dollar strengthened. Retail fund outflows accelerated.
Preferreds returned -0.50% with spreads at 212 bps. Retail par preferreds lagged while bank issues held up better.

sector_views.rationale: Nuveen favors longer-duration muni exposure over Treasuries, with muni yields at 4.29% and taxable muni yields attracting crossover buyers.
Credit fundamentals remain sound but spreads are widening, so the firm prefers high-quality bonds with attractive yields.
Weighed by equity selloff, heavy issuance and negative fund flows, though fundamentals are described as sound.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike expected in December 2026 and March 2027, then pause
macro_indicators.interpretation: Further tightening is expected, which supports front-end yields even amid safe-haven demand.
The yield is expected to stay near current levels this year and drift lower in 2027.
Front-end yields are expected to stay elevated, consistent with a hiking path then a pause.

trade_ideas.description: Favor longer-duration exposure in tax-exempt municipals rather than Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: Muni yields at 4.29% make longer duration attractive relative to Treasuries.

risk_factors: Equity selloff and S&P 500 correction could spread to credit through wider spreads.
Heavy new issuance in IG and high yield pressures spreads.
Fed hikes with strong inflation could lift yields if safe-haven demand fades.
Outflows from high yield and EM funds could accelerate.
vol_and_positioning: Equity volatility and heavy new issuance pushed IG spreads wider, though demand for new deals stayed solid.
High yield fund flows turned negative and EM retail fund outflows accelerated, signaling risk-off positioning in credit.
Senior loan flows were positive, led by CLO ETFs, and CLO and loan fund demand was steady.
